problem: The sign is wrong. If hs is a suction lift and hd is the delivery height, the cylinder pressure during suction is (patm − ρg hs) and during delivery it is (patm + ρg hd). So the pressure difference across the stroke, and hence the work per stroke, is ρg(hd + hs)AL, not ρg(hd − hs)AL. As written, a pump lifting water 4 m and delivering 20 m would show a total head of 16 m instead of 24 m.
fix: W = ρ g A L (h<sub>d</sub> + h<sub>s</sub>) and P = ρ g Q<sub>th</sub> (h<sub>d</sub> + h<sub>s</sub>) / 1000, where h<sub>d</sub> is the delivery height above the pump centre line and h<sub>s</sub> is the suction lift below it, both positive lengths in m. If a signed elevation is used (suction level below the datum taken as negative), the same result reads (h<sub>d</sub> − h<sub>s</sub>); state this convention.

problem: Wrong number. Slip fraction = 1 − C<sub>d</sub>, so C<sub>d</sub> = 0.92 means a slip fraction of 0.08, that is 8 % slip, not 12 %. The trap text states the opposite of the chapter's own quiz Q5, which correctly gets 8 %.
fix: C<sub>d</sub> and slip fraction add to one, so a C<sub>d</sub> of 0.92 and 8 % slip are the same statement (and a C<sub>d</sub> of 0.88 is 12 % slip).

problem: 'Both lines are wavy, flattest at mid-stroke where piston speed is highest' gives the wrong reason. The lines come closest to the ideal levels at mid-stroke because the acceleration of the water column is zero there, not because the piston is fastest. At mid-stroke the piston is fastest, so friction, not acceleration, is at its largest at that instant.
fix: Both lines are wavy. The suction line dips lowest and the delivery line peaks highest near the start of each stroke, where the water column's acceleration is greatest; at mid-stroke the acceleration is zero, so the lines come back closest to the ideal levels, held apart only by friction.

problem: The ratio of ideal power to actual (indicated) power is not the pump's overall efficiency. Overall efficiency is the water power actually delivered divided by the shaft power input, and it also carries the bearing, gland and seal losses that never appear on the indicator diagram.
fix: The motor must supply more power than ρ g Q<sub>th</sub> (h<sub>d</sub> + h<sub>s</sub>). The ratio of ideal area to actual indicator-diagram area measures only what is lost inside the cylinder; the pump's overall efficiency is the water power delivered (ρ g Q<sub>act</sub> × total head) divided by the shaft power input, which is smaller still.

problem: The extra area is said to be spent 'on accelerating the water column'. Work done against acceleration is stored in the moving water and given back during the deceleration half of the same stroke, so over a full stroke it adds nothing to the enclosed area.
fix: The extra area is net work lost to friction in the pipes, valves and piston; acceleration changes the shape of the lines but its work cancels out over a stroke.
